question.text: The increasing order of pKb for the following compounds will be :

solution.text: Compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">‘</mi><mo>’</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mo>’</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">’</mi></math> represents Guanidine, the conjugate acid of which is resonance stabilised. Compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>"</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>"</mo></math> is aliphatic amine, here the <math><mi mathvariant="normal">‘</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">’</mi></math> is <math><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> whereas in compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>'</mi><mi>'A</mi><mo>"</mo></math> the <math><mi mathvariant="normal">'</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">'</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">'</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">'</mi></mrow></msup></math> is <math><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> .
